faq.q: Does the $800,000 cap matter for the first-time home buyers' PTT exemption?
faq.a: Yes — in the buyer's favour. The program's full exemption runs to a fair market value of $835,000 (exempting the tax on the first $500,000 of the purchase price), with a partial exemption only between $835,000 and $860,000, provided the buyer and property meet all the program's other conditions — so a qualifying first-time buyer anywhere in this under-$800K band sits under the full-exemption value ceiling.

faq.q: Are 55+ age-restricted condos still legal in Chilliwack?
faq.a: Yes. Since November 24, 2022, 55+ is the only age restriction a BC strata bylaw may impose — any bylaw restricting occupancy to a younger age is invalid, and rental-restriction bylaws are not permitted at all; exemptions to 55+ bylaws cover caregivers, people already residing when the bylaw passed, children and younger spouses or partners.

faq.q: How does a condo buyer get out of Chilliwack without a car?
faq.a: BC Transit's Route 66 Fraser Valley Express serves Chilliwack, Abbotsford, Langley and Burnaby with daily service and is operated by Chilliwack Transit; local Chilliwack routes named in BC Transit's January 4, 2026 service changes include Route 51, Route 53 Fairfield and Route 57 Broadway.

faq.q: What should I read before buying a condo in Chilliwack?
faq.a: The Form B, the bylaws, the last two years of strata minutes, the depreciation report and the contingency reserve fund balance. They show planned repairs, special levies and rules on pets and rentals.

faq.q: What do strata fees cover on a condo in Chilliwack?
faq.a: Strata fees pay for upkeep and insurance of the common property and the contingency reserve fund, and in some buildings heat, hot water or other services. The Form B Information Certificate lists exactly what a unit's fee covers.
